title: Tibet mega-dam (Motuo) value chain
map_limitation: Chinese SOE procurement is opaque: supplier awards surface late and partially. A-share beneficiaries re-rated on announcement day (limit-ups, July 2025), so local crowdedness is already elevated; the mapping question is which links remain unpriced OUTSIDE China. Links are unscored by design — run heat to score them with fetched evidence.

links.name: Power offtake & load centers
links.role: Where ~300 TWh/yr lands from the early 2030s [Reuters/CNBC, as of 2025-07]: eastern load centers via long-haul transmission plus Tibet-local industry; the demand anchor that justifies everything upstream.

bottleneck.note: Offtake is policy-assured; the constraint is delivery infrastructure, not demand.

links.name: China Yajiang Group (project owner)
links.role: New state-owned entity created to lead the 1.2 trillion yuan ($167B) five-cascade development [Bloomberg/Reuters, as of 2025-07]; the order book every supplier link sells into.

bottleneck.note: Single buyer; procurement pace sets the entire chain's revenue timing.

links.name: Civil construction & EPC
links.role: Five cascade stations in a Himalayan gorge, >40M cubic meters of concrete [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; PowerChina and China Energy Engineering rose limit-up on announcement.

bottleneck.note: SOE EPC capacity is deep; margins bid-competed — the volume-without-capture trap likely applies (score it).

links.name: Tunneling & TBMs
links.role: The design diverts the river's great bend through headrace tunnels; hard-rock TBMs and drill-blast at extreme altitude are the schedule-critical works.

bottleneck.note: Few suppliers of large hard-rock TBMs (CRCHI, China Railway Engineering Equipment; Herrenknecht private); geology risk concentrates here.

links.name: Cement & materials at altitude
links.role: >16 million tons of cement implied [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; Tibet-local producers hold regional pricing power because hauling cement to Medog is prohibitive.

bottleneck.note: Regional quasi-monopoly (Xizang Tianlu named the major beneficiary); capacity vs 2030 schedule is the question.

links.name: Hydro turbines & generators
links.role: Dongfang Electric holds ~45% of China's conventional hydro equipment market and could take ~54B yuan of orders from this project alone [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; Harbin Electric is the other domestic heavyweight.

bottleneck.note: 60 GW of high-head units is a decade of duopoly-scale work; A-shares repriced immediately — H-share discounts are the screen question.

links.name: UHVDC transmission buildout
links.role: Moving ~60 GW from Medog to eastern load centers requires new ultra-high-voltage DC corridors: converter valves, transformers, and grid integration — the quieter industrial layer behind the turbine story.

bottleneck.note: UHVDC converter capability is concentrated in a handful of Chinese suppliers (NARI, XD Electric, TBEA); corridor siting and build time gates offtake.

links.name: Copper & conductors
links.role: Thousands of kilometers of HVDC lines plus 60 GW of machines add a marginal but global copper and aluminum-conductor demand leg — the most Western-investable raw-material angle.

bottleneck.note: Global commodity; this project moves sentiment more than balances — capture is the question, not availability.

links.name: Global hydro-equipment spillover
links.role: A decade of Chinese domestic hydro demand absorbs Chinese supplier capacity, tightening the global market Western utilities buy from (Andritz, Voith private, GE Vernova hydro) — the second-order link most accessible outside China.

bottleneck.note: Spillover thesis needs verification in Western hydro backlogs and pricing — a genuine run-heat question.

links.name: India's counter-buildout (Siang UMP)
links.role: India accelerated the 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (NHPC + NEEPCO, ~$10-13.2B, construction from ~2028) explicitly as a flood-buffer response to Medog [Wikipedia/EastMojo, as of 2026-03]; plus Assam flood-control works.

bottleneck.note: Land consent is the gating item (village MOUs signing through early 2026); Indian hydro EPC and NHPC are the direct exposure — T3 listings.

links.name: Riparian risk & monitoring
links.role: Downstream flow risk for India/Bangladesh creates durable demand for satellite hydrology monitoring, early-warning systems, and eventually parametric flood covers — thin today, but the least-priced Western angle on the whole event.

bottleneck.note: Nascent; demand is real (India built new monitoring posts post-announcement) but revenue concentration per listed name is unproven — score honestly.

notes.text: Built from the first UI click (run chain via the artifact queue).
